newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RONALDO SAYS HE OPEN TO TRANSFER TALKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO SAYS HE OPEN TO TRANSFER TALKS.

text.p: Brazil's Ronaldo, object of feverish transfer speculation, said on Sunday he was willing to talk to any club making him a serious offer but made clear that his heart remained with Barcelona.
"I just want this story to finish as soon as possible," Ronaldo told the Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper in an interview at his home in Spain.
"It has all become very boring. I will consider offers from other clubs but if Barcelona matches them I will always chose Barcelona. Even if they are great clubs," Ronaldo said.
Italian club Lazio has been repeatedly mentioned as a frontrunner to sign the striker.

Lazio coach Dino Zoff confirmed on Saturday that the club was chasing Ronaldo with reasonable grounds for optimism. President Sergio Cragnotti has said next month could see important developments in the affair.
The daily Corriere dello Sport said that Alexandre Martins, one of Ronaldo's agents, would be in Rome next week to meet Cragnotti and discuss the affair.
Ronaldo said, however, that his Spanish club had 105,000 members, the crowd gave him his strength and encouragement and that Barcelona was the right place "for now".
"Barcelona made me great. I was good at PSV (Eindhoven) but all this attention has come because I play for Barca," declared the Brazilian, who joined Barcelona from the Dutch club.
"I have a choice, it is a matter of lifestyle and atmosphere," he said.
However he said the Spanish club's failure to agree an improved contract had forced his hand.
"I am upset with the Barcelona leadership," he said.
"I am very disappointed, very...The Barcelona officials have pushed me into this situation. And there are offers."

Italian newspapers have reported that Barcelona are ready to let Ronaldo, the club's top goalscorer and the world player of the year, leave for $32 million and that Cragnotti has offered him a net annual salary of $4.2 million until 2005.
Ronaldo told the Gazzetta he knew Lazio were serious but he had never spoken to any club official. However several other clubs have also been reported to be interested, both in Italy and abroad.
The newspaper said at least two other Italian clubs and three others in Europe were making similar-sized bids to that of Lazio.
The Corriere said there were as many as seven clubs.
Bayern Munich in Germany and Manchester United have been mentioned along with AC Milan and Juventus.

Both Juventus owner Giovanni Agnelli and Milan boss Silvio Berlusconi, whose clubs have both been involved in some of the world's biggest transfers, have talked publicly of Ronaldo recently while apparently ruling out any offers.
Berlusconi said the amount asked was too high while Agnelli was quoted as telling Juventus players recently that they "would have to get used to winning without Ronaldo."
